Reasoning: Parallel straight wires attract each other when the current directions are the same, and repel each other when the current directions are opposite. e has the same current direction as c and d below, so c and d attract e respectively along two downward diagonals; their horizontal components cancel each other, and their vertical components are both downward. e has the opposite current direction to a and b above, so a and b repel e, causing e to move away from the upper left corner and the upper right corner respectively; the horizontal components of these two repulsive forces also cancel each other, and the vertical components are also both downward. After the four forces are combined, the resultant force on conductor e is downward.

raw_record.question_text: As shown in Figure 3, conductors \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), \(d\), and \(e\) are straight conductors carrying the same current. Conductors \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), and \(d\) are located at the four vertices of a square, and conductor \(e\) is located at the center. What is the direction of the electromagnetic force experienced by conductor \(e\)?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: e is centered in the square, with a and b above it carrying current into the page, and c and d below it carrying current out of the page like e. Since e and c/d have the same current direction, c and d attract e along the two downward diagonals; their horizontal components cancel, leaving a downward component. Since e and a/b have opposite current directions, a and b repel e away from the two upper corners; those repulsion directions also have downward components, and their horizontal components cancel. Adding all four contributions gives a net force on e downward.
